title: Two Dockerfiles: build -f
summary: Add a Dockerfile.dev next to the real one, build it with -f, and edit the app live in a dev container.

tasks.title: `greet-f:1.0` is built from the unchanged `Dockerfile`
tasks.hint: Leave `Dockerfile` as it is. `docker build -t greet-f:1.0 .` uses it, because that's the name Docker looks for.

tasks.title: `greet-f:dev` is built from `Dockerfile.dev`: light yellow, with `--watch`
tasks.hint: Make `Dockerfile.dev`: copy the Dockerfile's lines, change `ENV COLOR=lightblue` to `ENV COLOR=lightyellow` and the last line to `CMD ["--watch", "app.js"]`. Then `docker build -f Dockerfile.dev -t greet-f:dev .`

tasks.title: `greet-dev` runs `greet-f:dev` on `http://localhost:3406`, with this folder mounted on `/app`
You changed `Hello` to `Hi` in `app.js`, and the page shows it without a rebuild
tasks.hint: Edit the `<h1>` line in `app.js`, save, and reload the page. `--watch` restarts the app when the file changes; the bind mount lets it see your file. `docker logs greet-dev` shows the restart.
